appraisal_events.evidence: « Allons, Gilberte, viens ; qu'est-ce que tu fais », cria d'une voix perçante et autoritaire une dame en blanc... l'impression laissée en moi par le ton despotique avec lequel la mère de Gilberte lui avait parlé sans qu'elle répliquât, en me la montrant comme forcée d'obéir à quelqu'un, comme n'étant pas supérieure à tout.
appraisal_events.explanation: Witnessed by the narrator, Gilberte's mother commands her sharply and Gilberte obeys without answering back; this punctures the narrator's image of Gilberte as untouchably superior, momentarily calming his anguish.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Ce pauvre Swann, quel rôle ils lui font jouer : on le fait partir pour qu'elle reste seule avec son Charlus, car c'est lui, je l'ai reconnu ! Et cette petite, mêlée à toute cette infamie ! »
appraisal_events.explanation: The grandfather pities Swann as a manipulated dupe, sidelined so his wife can stay with her presumed lover Charlus, and explicitly casts Gilberte as tainted by association with this scandal.

appraisal_events.evidence: Ainsi passa près de moi ce nom de Gilberte, donné comme un talisman... imprégnant, irisant la zone d'air pur qu'il avait traversée... du mystère de la vie de celle qu'il désignait... le charme dont son nom avait encensé cette place... allait gagner, enduire, embaumer tout ce qui l'approchait, ses grands-parents..., la sublime profession d'agent de change, le douloureux quartier des Champs-Élysées.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's infatuation transforms Gilberte's very name into a talisman that magically elevates her and everything associated with her, in language whose hyperbole (a stockbroker's profession called 'sublime') signals the adult narrator's gentle irony about the child's idealization even as it conveys its genuine intensity.

status_effects.explanation: Shown obeying her mother's despotic tone without reply, Gilberte briefly loses the aura of supremacy the narrator had attributed to her.
Her piercing, authoritative command produces immediate silent compliance from Gilberte, a small display of verbal command winning out.
The grandfather's exclamation of pity frames Swann as a manipulated, humiliated figure, sidelined from his own household.
The grandfather explicitly names her as mixed up in the household's 'infamie', a separate and negative judgment distinct from the narrator's own idealization of her.
The grandfather's remark implies she has arranged to be left alone with Charlus, casting her conduct in a discrediting light.

The narrator's sustained, talismanic idealization of her name and everything near her constitutes a clear, if lightly ironized, local elevation, distinct from the grandfather's separate negative judgment.

ambiguities: The speaker addressed as Gilberte's mother is resolved to Odette via the reference sheet's documented mother-daughter relation ('la fille de Odette'), since the passage itself never names her directly, only as 'une dame en blanc' and 'la mère de Gilberte'.

Charlus is named and implicated in the grandfather's remark about Swann's marginalization, but the passage does not evaluate him directly in his own right, so no status effect is recorded for him despite his inclusion as a materially involved figure.
